title: Interview with Vladislav Ursu!
excerpt: Setka Cup interviewed Moldova’s number one player – Vladislav Ursu!
body_html:
Interview with Vladislav Ursu about his “ticket” to the Olympic Games

1️⃣ Tell us honestly: did you expect to become the first table tennis player from Moldova to take part in the Olympic Games?
I didn’t expect to reach the Olympics so soon, this year, since I’m still only 23 and a table tennis player’s peak is at 27-31. But I believed in myself, because I had already beaten top-level players like these at other international competitions.

2️⃣ Who called you first to congratulate you?
Of course, the first people to congratulate me were my girlfriend, who was there in the hall, and my teammate Andrei Puțuntica. And my parents were among the first to call — congratulating me and crying.

3️⃣ How hard was it to win, and what was harder: overcoming yourself mentally, or physically playing at your best?
Winning was harder mentally, especially in the final, when I realised this was my chance and I had to make the most of it. It was also mentally demanding that no one from Moldova had ever played table tennis at the Olympics, and that I could become the first and make history.

4️⃣ Who or what helped you achieve such an incredible result?
The support of my loved ones and my coach, and also the Polish federation, which helped me prepare well. I go to training camps with very strong players from their national team to prepare for competitions.

5️⃣ How did you prepare for the qualification? Was it different from preparing for any other competition?
The training took place in Poland, with players from the national team. There were two or three sessions a day. We worked on tactics against the leading players in this tournament. Preparing for important competitions is always different from normal training: there is more work at the table, physical endurance training, and we also train tactics. What influences the result most is self-belief, training with strong players under a smart coach who breaks down the whole game — and the atmosphere among the players during preparation matters a lot too.
